title: Cooking Videos Speak Every Language — Does Yours?
description: Recipe content travels further than any other YouTube niche, yet most food channels stay stuck in one language. How AI dubbing opens the rest up.
excerpt: Food needs no translation. Your voiceover does — and that's what's keeping your channel inside one border.
content:
Recipe videos are the second most-watched category on YouTube after music. Everyone eats, and a shot of butter hitting a hot pan reads the same in Ohio as it does in Osaka. So why do most food channels never leave their home market? It isn't the food. It's the narration.

## Subtitles fail in the kitchen

Nobody watches a recipe sitting still. Their hands are in dough, something is sizzling, and the phone is propped against a canister two feet away. If the only way to follow along is reading text, they bounce. That's why dubbed cooking videos consistently hold viewers longer than subtitled ones — you can listen while you cook, you can't read while you cook.

## One shoot, seven markets

AI dubbing now carries your actual voice, pacing and inflection into another language. [TubeVoice](https://tubevoice.io) dubs a finished video into 50+ languages, so one afternoon in the kitchen becomes a German, Spanish and Polish version too. No reshoot, no relighting, no hiring voice actors.

Start with what already works. Open YouTube Studio, pull your three best-performing recipes from the last year, and dub those first. You're not gambling on new content — you're taking proven content to a bigger pond.

## The revenue math

Food CPMs in Germany or the US run several times higher than in smaller markets. A dubbed upload often out-earns two brand-new videos, and it's already shot and edited. Add the novelty factor: a regional dish that's ordinary at home is genuinely interesting abroad.

Pick one archive hit, dub it into two languages, and give it a month. The analytics will tell you whether to keep going. They usually do.
